summary: Brahma 1.1.0 (docs/decisions.md Rounds 17-20): show the conversation between You, Brahma, Codex and Claude as one timed chat in the terminal UI and in `brahma run` output, with every displayed time in the system timezone; and give Brahma six-field work reports (Completed, Evidence, Current work, Next work, Where we are, Needs you) after each task and at the end of each run, following a mirrored `work-report` skill. Stored events, `brahma events` and existing --json fields stay as they are; `brahma --json status` gains an additive `report` field.

tasks.title: Chat renderer and local time formatting
tasks.instructions: Create src/brahma/chat.py: a pure display module that turns stored events (models.Event plus its stored `created` UTC ISO time) into chat messages, with no I/O, no provider calls and no change to how events are stored. Speakers: provider brahma with role user -> 'You'; other brahma events -> 'Brahma'; codex -> 'Codex'; claude -> 'Claude'. A message may name who it is for ('Brahma -> Claude', 'Codex -> Claude'); Codex and Claude never message each other directly (Brahma relays a reviewer's findings in the builder's next brief), so an arrow shows the addressee, not a direct channel. Translate every known event kind into one plain sentence from its speaker: task_state (assigned, building, checking, reviewing, ready, blocked, waiting, incomplete, with the task number and title), routing (who was chosen and why, one line), model_selected, progress (the worker's own words), check and checks_failing (counts and which check), review_notes / reviewer verdicts (verdict, number of findings, each finding id, severity, path and text, addressed to the builder), dispute_* events, wait (provider and reset time), approval/approved/user/user_note/dispute_decision/capacity_confirmed from the user (speaker You), publication, origin_baseline (one Brahma message 'Recorded the repository's push target for this session', with no URL or hash; if the event marks the session as legacy, say that its result requires manual publication), ready_receipt (one line, no JSON), work_report (introduced by task 2: JSON with the keys completed, evidence, current_work, next_work, where_we_are, needs_you; render it as one Brahma message with six labelled rows in that order), summary, error, warning, information, enforcement, restore, context_expansion, note_applied, signin_lost, verification_spent, outcome. Hide from the chat: usage (it belongs to the status bar), native_session, plan and plan_created JSON, and quota events that repeat the previous quota state of the same provider (show the first and any change, as one sentence). Any other kind gets a short readable fallback ('Brahma: <kind> recorded'), never raw JSON. Every displayed text passes the existing redaction boundary (safety.redact) and the existing displayable cleaning of control, C1 and Unicode format characters; multi-line worker text may keep its line breaks. Times: format with the system timezone (datetime.astimezone() / time.localtime, tzname from the system), e.g. '14:38 IST'; show the full date ('Sat 21 Nov 2026') on the first message and whenever the local day changes; helper functions for a time, a date-time and a reset time are public so other modules reuse them. Write tests in tests/test_chat.py; make them deterministic by setting the TZ environment variable and calling time.tzset() (restore afterwards), covering Asia/Kolkata and at least one other zone. Add a test that scans src/brahma for every event kind string emitted (Event(... kind ...) and _emit(emit, "kind", ...)) and fails if a kind has neither a chat rule nor an explicit hidden entry. Tests must never launch the real claude or codex CLIs and must import tests.provider_guard like the other tests.
acceptance: chat.py renders every event kind emitted in src/brahma or lists it as hidden, and a test enforces this
An origin_baseline event says that the push target was recorded and exposes neither the fingerprint nor raw JSON
A work_report event renders as one Brahma message with six labelled rows in the fixed order
Speakers are You, Brahma, Codex and Claude; addressed messages show the addressee
No raw JSON appears in any rendered chat message
Repeated identical quota events are shown once; usage, native_session, plan and plan_created are hidden
Times use the system timezone with its abbreviation; the full date appears on the first message and on each local day change
Rendered text is redacted and stripped of control, C1 and Unicode format characters
Stored events and their JSON are not changed
Tests pass deterministically under TZ=Asia/Kolkata and another timezone, without launching provider CLIs
Legacy origin baseline events explain that publication for those sessions is manual

  When the events are rendered in order
  Then exactly one quota sentence is shown and the usage event shows nothing

Scenario: the owner's own actions appear as You
  Given the approval event "Approved by the device owner: contract ee24ddff..."
  When the event is rendered

  When it is rendered
  Then Brahma says it recorded the push target for this session
  And neither the fingerprint nor raw JSON appears

tasks.title: Brahma's six-field work reports and the mirrored work-report skill
tasks.instructions: Write the work-report skill once and mirror it byte for byte at .claude/skills/work-report/SKILL.md and .agents/skills/work-report/SKILL.md (same frontmatter style as .claude/skills/brahma-grill-me/SKILL.md). Its rules, addressed to the owner with no person's name or project: after every finished task or handoff item, report in this order: Completed (what was finished, its resulting behaviour, and the commit reference), Evidence (measured test results or scores, with their scope and what is still unverified), Current work (the task being worked on now), Next work (the next task in the agreed order), Where we are (position in the plan, readiness, and reviews still owed), Needs you (a specific decision for the owner, or "None"); report significant problems immediately; give brief progress updates during longer work; expand only when a failure or a decision needs explanation; keep implementation, tests, measured results, independent review and release status distinct; a passing code test is never a claimed ability. Create src/brahma/report.py: build a report (a dict with exactly the keys completed, evidence, current_work, next_work, where_we_are, needs_you, all strings) only from what Brahma recorded for the current plan (events since the latest plan_created): task_state transitions, the checks Brahma ran (command and result), the reviewer's provider, verdict and findings by severity, ownership verification, the local commit, the ready receipt and the publication outcome. Never copy a worker's claims into Evidence; say what is unverified (for example no checks configured, or a review is a model's judgement). Needs you names the concrete action (brahma decide for a disputed review, resume after a pause or the kill switch, the provider and reset time for a quota wait, a new plan when the attempt budget is exhausted) or "None". In src/brahma/session.py: after a task_state event whose state is ready, blocked, incomplete, waiting, needs_decision or cancelled is stored, and once after the run's summary event, emit Event(kind="work_report") whose text is the report as JSON. This is best effort: a failure to build or store a report is swallowed and never changes the run's status, its job, its commit, its receipt or its publication; do not change any other behaviour of session.py. Add a public function in report.py that returns the latest stored report of a session (or None), for task 3. Tests in tests/test_report.py: field order and keys; evidence from recorded checks and reviews only (a worker's 'all tests pass' text never appears in Evidence); Needs you for each waiting/blocked/decision case; a report failure leaves the run's outcome unchanged; the two SKILL.md files are byte-identical. Tests must never launch the real claude or codex CLIs.
acceptance: The two work-report SKILL.md files exist, are byte-identical, name no person or project, and state the six fields, their order and the rules
Brahma stores a work_report event after each task ends and once at the end of each run
Each report has exactly the six fields in order, built only from recorded facts
Evidence never contains a worker's own claims and states what is unverified
Needs you names a concrete action or says None
A failure to build or store a report never changes the run's status, job, commit, receipt or publication
No other behaviour of session.py changes
Tests pass without launching provider CLIs
scenarios:
Scenario: a ready task gets a report
  Given task 1 ended ready after Brahma's checks passed and the reviewer passed it
  When the task_state event is stored
  Then a work_report event follows whose Evidence names the checks Brahma ran and the reviewer's verdict
  And whose Next work names task 2

Scenario: a disputed review needs the owner
  Given task 1 is waiting for the owner's decision on a disputed high finding
  When its report is built
  Then Needs you names brahma decide for that session

Scenario: a quota wait names the reset
  Given task 2 is waiting for Codex until Wed 25 Nov 2026 21:40 IST
  When its report is built
  Then Needs you names Codex and that reset time

Scenario: a worker's claim is not evidence
  Given the builder wrote "all tests pass" and Brahma ran no checks
  When the report is built
  Then Evidence says no checks were run and does not repeat the claim

Scenario: a report failure changes nothing
  Given building the report raises an error
  When the task ends ready
  Then the run's status, job, commit and receipt are as without reports

Scenario: the run ends with a report
  Given a run of two tasks ends
  When its summary event is stored
  Then one more work_report covers the whole run

tasks.title: Show the chat and the reports everywhere a person reads the conversation
tasks.instructions: Use src/brahma/chat.py (task 1) and src/brahma/report.py (task 2) without editing them, everywhere a person reads the conversation or a time. src/brahma/ui.py: replace the three conversation panes (#manager, #codex, #claude) with one shared chat timeline in time order, each message coloured by speaker (keep the existing colours for Brahma, Codex and Claude; add one for You); keep the status bar, controls and slash commands working; usage still updates the status bar. src/brahma/cli.py: the stderr `log` callback of `brahma run` prints chat lines (time, speaker, optional addressee, text) instead of '[provider/role] text'; use colour only when stderr is a terminal and NO_COLOR is unset. src/brahma/board.py and src/brahma/usage.py: show reset and observation times in the system timezone via chat.py's helpers instead of UTC. Add a `report` field to `brahma --json status` (the latest work report's six fields, or null) and show the latest report in the human `brahma status` output. Do not change any other --json field, `brahma events` (JSON lines), exit codes, stored events, stored timestamps (UTC) or the approval screen's contract text. Update the existing tests that assert the old display (tests/test_ui.py pane ids and layout, tests/test_review11.py _pane_entries, tests/test_usage.py 'UTC') to the new behaviour without weakening what they protect (redaction at the rendering boundary, narrow-terminal layout). Add tests/test_chat_display.py for the CLI log lines, the TUI timeline and local reset times, deterministic via TZ and time.tzset(). Tests must never launch the real claude or codex CLIs. As part of integration, set the package and CLI version to 1.1.0, update uv.lock to match, and record the chat and reports in the 1.1.0 changelog entry.
acceptance: The terminal UI shows one shared chat timeline with speakers You, Brahma, Codex and Claude
`brahma run` prints chat lines with local times, and no raw JSON, to stderr
Colour is used only on a terminal and never when NO_COLOR is set
Usage resets and the board show local times with the timezone abbreviation
`brahma --json status` has a `report` field with the latest six-field report or null; no other JSON field changes
--json outputs, `brahma events`, exit codes, stored events and the approval contract text are unchanged
Existing tests are updated without weakening redaction or the narrow-terminal behaviour
Tests pass deterministically without launching provider CLIs
The changelog, lockfile, package metadata and Brahma CLI all report version 1.1.0
